turns.t: Morning. I've had a temperature a couple of days and the wife said get it checked. Tick bite, last week.
Right. Where was the bite and how did you spot it? ~
Back of my knee. Was walking the dog on the moor. Found it in the bath, pulled it off with tweezers. ~
Good that you got it off. When did the temperature start?
Two days ago. I've felt hot and cold. Sweating at night.
Have you measured it?
Thirty-eight point four, last night.
Anything else along with it? ~
Not really. A bit achy, nowt else. ~
Right. And any long-term illnesses I should know about?
Asthma, since I was a lad. Nowt bad.
Let me take your temperature and pulse. ~
Go on. ~
Temperature 38.1, pulse 96.
So I've got one. ~
You have. Let me see the bite site. Turn round. ~
It's just a little scab.
I've had a look and it's healing well. Nothing spreading around it that I can see. ~
So what's your thinking? ~
A fever a week after a tick bite means I'd think of Lyme disease, though it could just be a virus, so I'm treating Lyme disease as a possibility, not a certainty.
What's the treatment? ~
I'm not starting anything today. We'll see how it behaves first. ~
Is that wise? ~
With only a fever and no rash, yes. Treatment for Lyme is a course of tablets, and I'd rather not give it unless it's needed. ~
Right. And what do I do meanwhile? ~
Rest, plenty of fluids, and keep taking your temperature morning and night. Write the numbers down.
Fair enough. ~
If the fever hasn't gone in two days, or a rash appears, or your joints swell, come back and see me that day.
Understood. And if it gets worse at the weekend? ~
Ring the out-of-hours number and say you've had a tick bite. They'll know.
Right then. Thanks. ~
Look after yourself. ~
